items.title: The real type-A Soergel category by scalar extension
items.statement: Extend Q→R and set S=R[x_1,...,x_n] with deg x_i=2, with the place-permuting S_n action. The Hodge page uses the coordinate/length normalization of the published reflection realization: alpha_i here means beta_i=x_i-x_{i+1}, and alpha_i^vee means beta_i^vee, so adjacent Cartan entries are -1. The published alternating balanced roots eps_i beta_i are used for diagrammatic presentations, not for positivity on this page. Both choices have identical reflections, invariant rings and underlying bimodules. Define B_i^R=S⊗_{S^{s_i}}S(1) and the real Soergel category as the idempotent completion of their finite additive graded tensor closure, with the same shifts as the rational category. Its unit is the graded ring S (as an object in cohomological degree zero), not a polynomial ring concentrated in internal degree zero. For a rational bimodule M write M^R=M⊗_Q R; the generator and Bott-Samelson constructions extend in this way. Standard graph supports, Delta/nabla flags and characters use the formulas of the rational page over R; the Hecke algebra remains the same integral normalized algebra. The dominant chamber is Theta={rho=Σ c_j x_j: c_i>c_{i+1} for all i}. It is nonempty, for example c_j=(n+1)/2-j.
items.strategy: The place permutation action and coordinate roots/coroots are explicitly supplied by the published two-normalization realization. We fix the coordinate choice for every alpha, Demazure trace and positivity condition on this Hodge page. The invariant-ring tensor bimodules do not change when a root is multiplied by -1; only the chosen Demazure/trace normalization changes, so no diagrammatic presentation is silently reinterpreted. The polynomial ring has S_0=R and finite-dimensional homogeneous pieces. Flat extension of Q to R commutes with the finite free presentations, invariant decomposition S=S^{s_i}⊕alpha_i S^{s_i}, shifts and tensor products. The idempotent closure is the defined real category; preservation of rational indecomposable labels is proved separately in the comparison lemma. For rho=Σ c_jx_j, rho(alpha_i^vee)=c_i-c_{i+1}; the displayed decreasing coefficients give value 1 at every simple coroot. These are the positive roots x_a-x_b for a<b used by inversion length, with adjacent Cartan entries -1. No alternating-sign dominant chamber or unverified replacement of rho is used.

items.title: The Hecke trace form, its values on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, and the standard pairing
items.statement: Let H = H_v(n) be the normalized type-A Hecke algebra over A = Z[v^{\pm1}] and let a be the A-linear anti-involution with a(v) = v, a(H_x) = H_{x^{-1}} (the reversal anti-involution of the Hecke page). Define the trace eps: H -> A by eps(H_w) = delta_{e,w} on the standard basis, and the bilinear form (-,-): H x H -> A by (h,h') := eps(a(h)h'). Then: (1) eps and (-,-) are well defined (the H_w are an A-basis); (2) (ph, qh') = pq(h,h') for p,q in A; (3) (hH_s, h') = (h, h'H_s) and (H_sh, h') = (h, H_sh') for all h,h' and all simple reflections s; (4) the standard basis is orthonormal, (H_x,H_y) = delta_{xy}; (5) on the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, (H_x,H_y) in vZ[v] for x != y and (H_x,H_x) in 1 + vZ[v]; (6) the same form is the standard pairing <H_x,H_y> = delta_{xy} used in the type-A Soergel Hom formula, transported through the identification of the normalized standard bases. All statements are integral and use no choice.
items.strategy: First give the normalized standard basis its A-bilinear dot product. On each pair {H_w,H_ws} with ell(ws)=ell(w)+1, right multiplication by H_s has matrix [[0,1],[1,v^{-1}-v]], symmetric for this product; the same holds for left multiplication on {H_w,H_sw}. Thus both generator actions are self-adjoint. Repeated adjunction of the factors of a reduced H_x gives (H_x,H_y)_dot=(1,a(H_x)H_y)_dot=eps(a(H_x)H_y). This proves standard orthonormality and identifies the trace-defined form with the dot product, including bilinearity and the generator-adjunction identities. If underline H_x=Σ_u h_{u,x}H_u and underline H_y=Σ_u h_{u,y}H_u, the form is Σ_u h_{u,x}h_{u,y}: there is no coefficient conjugation, since the form and reversal anti-involution are A-linear. Each diagonal coefficient h_{x,x}=1, every off-top coefficient is in vZ[v], and unavailable coefficients are zero. Thus when x≠y every product has at least one factor divisible by v; for x=y the unique constant term is 1. This proves the KL trace properties without any positivity theorem. The same orthonormal standard pairing is the published Hom-formula pairing in the normalized Hecke dictionary.

items.title: Indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodules are classified by their normalized top support
items.statement: Over $k=\mathbb Q$ or $k=\mathbb R$, the bimodule Soergel category has unique finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions. For every $x\in S_n$ there is a unique normalized indecomposable $B_x$ supported on $\{y:y\le x\}$ with top $\Delta$ layer exactly $\Delta_x=R_x(-\ell(x))$. It is the unique summand with the $x$ graph of any reduced Bott-Samelson word for $x$. Every indecomposable is exactly one $B_x(d)$. Its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local, with residue field $k$ under restriction to its rank-one top layer. No Kazhdan-Lusztig character identity is assumed.
items.strategy: Local supplier-first reconstruction of the complete argument in the carrier; no diagrammatic equivalence or character conjecture used.

items.title: Normalized type-A Soergel bimodules are self-dual and have length degree bounds
items.statement: Over $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$, let $B_x$ be the normalized indecomposable bimodule classified by its top support. With right dual $DM=\operatorname{Hom}_{-R}^{\bullet}(M,R)$, one has $DB_x\cong B_x$. Its right reduction has degrees only in $[-\ell(x),\ell(x)]$, all congruent to $\ell(x)$ modulo two, and the two extremal dimensions are one. Hence its reduced graded dimensions are symmetric. Every Bott-Samelson word has a graded perfect symmetric invariant trace form. These assertions assume neither the Kazhdan-Lusztig character conjecture nor hard Lefschetz.

items.title: The reduced Soergel module and the dominant Lefschetz operator
items.statement:
**The reduction.** Work over the ring $S=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ of the real
scalar-extension definition ([[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]]),
with $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ the ideal of positive-degree elements; the residue
field of the right action is
$$k:=S/S_+=\mathbb R,$$
with quotient map $S\twoheadrightarrow k$, $s\mapsto \bar s$. For a graded
$(S,S)$-bimodule $M$ that is finite free as a right $S$-module put
$$\overline M:=M\otimes_Sk=M/MS_+,$$
the **reduction** of $M$: a finite-dimensional graded $k$-vector space, on which
the left $S$-action descends because $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $MS_+$ is
stable under left multiplication. Write $\overline M^{\,i}$ for its homogeneous
component of degree $i$, $d_i(M):=\dim_{\mathbb R}\overline M^{\,i}$ for the
graded dimensions, and
$$\dim\overline M:=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}d_i(M)\,v^{-i}$$
for the **graded dimension** (a finite Laurent polynomial); all tensor products
below are over $S$. For a morphism $f:M\to M'$ of graded bimodules, i.e. a
degree-zero bi-$S$-linear map, the induced map
$$\overline f:\overline M\to\overline{M'},\qquad \overline f(m+MS_+):=f(m)+M'S_+ ,$$
is well defined and $k$-linear of degree zero, because $f(MS_+)\subseteq M'S_+$.
Reduction is a functor from finite right-free graded bimodules to finite
dimensional graded $k$-vector spaces; it preserves finite direct sums and
shifts, in the sense $\overline{M(d)}=\overline M(d)$ in the Elias-Williamson
shift convention $M(d)_e=M_{d+e}$.

**The dominant Lefschetz operator.** Fix a strictly dominant degree-two
element
$$\rho=\sum_{j=1}^nc_jx_j\in S_2,\qquad c_1>c_2>\cdots>c_n ,$$
which exists by [[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]] (for
example $c_j=(n+1)/2-j$); recall that this is exactly the condition
$\rho(\alpha_i^\vee)>0$ for every simple coroot $\alpha_i^\vee$ in the
coordinate normalization of this page
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]). Let
$\rho\cdot(-):M\to M$, $m\mapsto\rho m$, denote left multiplication by $\rho$.
Since $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $\rho\,(MS_+)\subseteq MS_+$, this
operator preserves the submodule $MS_+$ and therefore descends to a degree-two
$k$-linear endomorphism
$$L_0:=\rho\cdot(-):\overline M\longrightarrow\overline M,\qquad m+MS_+\longmapsto \rho m+MS_+,$$
called the **dominant Lefschetz operator** on $\overline M$. For rational
objects $B_x,B_s$ with real scalar extensions
$B_x^R=B_x\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$ and $B_s^R$, the same construction
applies to the reduced tensor product
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}=\overline{(B_xB_s)^R}$, where $B_xB_s$ denotes the
tensor product over the rational polynomial ring; the operator $L_0$ on it is
the value $\zeta=0$ of the deformed operator $L_\zeta$ defined later on this
page.

**Descent detection.** For every $w\in S_n$ and every simple reflection $s_i$
one has
$$(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ell(s_iw)>\ell(w).$$
Indeed, $(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}$ is positive
exactly when $w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1)$, the left-ascent criterion for inversion
length. Thus the displayed evaluation detects left descents; applied to
$w=x^{-1}$ it detects right descents of $x$, because $\ell(s_ix^{-1})=\ell(xs_i)$.

**Grading conventions.** The reduced module $\overline{B_x^R}$ has bottom degree
$-\ell(x)$ and top degree $+\ell(x)$; the unreduced bimodule has nonzero
components in arbitrarily high degrees. On a reduced module the "centered" degree $-i$ is the
internal degree $-i$, and the Lefschetz operator raises internal degree by two.
All homological (complex) shifts are written $[\,j\,]$ and all internal shifts
$(d)$, as on the rest of this page; the Bruhat order used throughout is the
rank-inequality order of
[[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]].
items.strategy: For a finite right-free bimodule M, reduction is M/(M S_+) and has finite graded dimension equal to its right rank. Left multiplication preserves this submodule and descends. In the coordinate normalization rho=Σ c_jx_j with c_1>...>c_n, (w rho)(alpha_i^vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}, positive exactly when w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1), equivalently ell(s_iw)>ell(w). This elementary inversion criterion proves the stated sign identity directly, and with w=x^{-1} gives the positive coefficient (x^{-1}rho)(alpha_s^vee) when xs>x. The alternating balanced coroots of the diagrammatic presentation are not used in this criterion.

items.title: Indecomposable labels, characters and filtration ranks agree after real scalar extension
items.statement: Let $B_w$ be the rational indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule and let $B_w^R$ be its real scalar extension. (1) $B_w^R$ is indecomposable; its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local with residue field $\mathbb R$. If $S(w)$ holds, its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is $\mathbb R$, but no rank-one assertion for the full graded endomorphism module is made. (2) Real extension preserves the labels and shifts of all finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions of rational Soergel bimodules, and every real indecomposable is a unique $B_w^R(d)$. (3) $\Delta$/$\nabla$ support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reduction by positive-degree right polynomials, and Hom spaces commute with scalar extension; thus character identities over $\mathbb R$ descend to $\mathbb Q$. (4) If $xs>x$ and $S(y)$ holds for all $y<xs$, then $B_xB_s=B_{xs}\oplus\bigoplus_{y<xs}B_y^{a_y}$ with $a_y$ nonnegative integers and no grading shifts; the top summand occurs once. If $xs<x$ and $S(x)$ holds, then $B_xB_s=B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$. All assertions concern the normalized self-dual indecomposables.
items.strategy: First justify base change of Hom by viewing it in a fixed degree as the kernel of the finitely many Q-linear equations expressing compatibility with the left and right polynomial generators. Finite graded right-free presentations and flatness of Q→R commute with these kernels. Support cuts are kernels of annihilator-ideal multiplication maps; the finite support flags split as right modules, so scalar extension also commutes with their quotients, ranks and reduction. For absolute indecomposability put A=End^0_Q(B_w), finite dimensional and local by the published Krull-Schmidt classification. Restrict endomorphisms to the unique rank-one top-support layer: this is a unital algebra map A→Q, surjective because scalar identities restrict to all scalars. Its kernel is the unique maximal ideal J of A; it is nilpotent. To justify nilpotence locally, the descending chain J^k stabilizes in finite dimension and the elementary Nakayama argument applied to its stable term forces that term to be zero: a minimal finite A-generating set for a nonzero stable term cannot exist, since expressing its last generator as a J-linear combination of those generators and inverting 1 minus its last coefficient eliminates that generator. Hence A⊗R has nilpotent ideal J⊗R with quotient R; every element outside that ideal is invertible by a finite geometric series after choosing its scalar lift. Thus A⊗R is local and B_w^R is indecomposable. Decomposing rational Bott-Samelson sums and applying finite Krull-Schmidt uniqueness over R proves the real classification and label comparison. Under S(w), the Hom formula and the constant-term property of the KL trace pairing give End^0(B_w^R)=R; the graded rank is (H_w,H_w), generally not 1. For (4), top support gives B_xs once and only shifted B_y with y<xs otherwise. Since ch(B_xB_s)=H_x H_s=H_xs+Σ μ_y H_y, the Hom formula and the trace-pairing lemma give Hom^j(B_y,B_xB_s)=0 for j<0 whenever y<xs. A summand B_y(d) would give a nonzero map B_y→B_xB_s(-d), forcing d≤0. Self-duality gives the paired shift -d, forcing d≥0. Thus d=0. For a descent, ch(B_xB_s)=(v+v^{-1})H_x=(v+v^{-1})ch(B_x); injectivity of the character on the split Grothendieck group and Krull-Schmidt uniqueness give the displayed two shifts.

items.title: The trace, the invariant intersection form on Bott-Samelson bimodules and its reduction
items.statement:
**The Bott-Samelson bimodule and its subexpression basis.** Fix a finite word
$\underline x=s_1\cdots s_m$ in the simple reflections and let
$$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x):=B_{s_1}\otimes_S\cdots\otimes_SB_{s_m}$$
be the real Bott-Samelson bimodule
([[def-bott-samelson-bimodule-of-a-word]]), with $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$
([[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]]). In each factor put
$$c_{\mathrm{id}}:=1\otimes1,\qquad c_s:=\tfrac12\bigl(\alpha_s\otimes1+1\otimes\alpha_s\bigr),$$
of degrees $-1$ and $+1$; here $\alpha_s$ is the coordinate root of
[[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]], so that
$\partial_s(r)=(r-sr)/\alpha_s$ is the coordinate Demazure operator. The
elements $\{c_{\mathrm{id}},c_s\}$ form a right (and a left) $S$-basis of $B_s$
and the multiplication rules
$$c_{\mathrm{id}}c_{\mathrm{id}}=c_{\mathrm{id}},\qquad c_{\mathrm{id}}c_s=c_s,\qquad c_sc_s=c_s\alpha_s$$
hold. For a subexpression $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_m)$
with $\varepsilon_i\in\{\mathrm{id},s_i\}$ put
$$c_\varepsilon:=c_{\varepsilon_1}\cdots c_{\varepsilon_m}\in\mathrm{BS}(\underline x),$$
the tensor product of the chosen elements, and put
$$c_{\mathrm{top}}:=c_{s_1}\cdots c_{s_m}.$$
The elements $\{c_\varepsilon\}$ form a right (and a left) $S$-basis of
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$; the bimodule is finite free of rank $2^m$ on each
side ([[lem-type-a-soergel-generators-are-finite-free-on-both-sides]]).
Moreover $\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)\cong\bigl(S\otimes_{S^{s_1}}S\otimes_{S^{s_2}}\cdots\otimes_{S^{s_m}}S\bigr)(m)$,
so after the shift by $(-m)$ the termwise multiplication makes
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)(-m)$ a commutative ring with unit $c_{\mathrm{id}}\cdots c_{\mathrm{id}}$;
in particular it contains the powers of any degree-two element and products of
commuting elements.

**The trace and the intersection form.** Define the **trace**
$$\operatorname{Tr}:\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)\longrightarrow S$$
to be the coefficient of $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ when an element is written in the
right basis $\{c_\varepsilon\}$, and define the **intersection form** by
$$\langle b,b'\rangle:=\operatorname{Tr}(b\,b'),$$
the product being taken in the commutative ring $\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)(-m)$.
Then:

1. $\langle-,-\rangle$ is a graded symmetric form, $S$-bilinear for the right
   action, and invariant in the sense
   $\langle rb,b'\rangle=\langle b,rb'\rangle$ and
   $\langle br,b'\rangle=\langle b,b'r\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle r$ for
   $r\in S$;
2. if $B$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of
   Bott-Samelson bimodules, then an invariant form on $B$ is obtained by
   restricting an invariant form of the ambient finite sum, and the restriction
   is determined up to the choices of the ambient forms;
3. for a self-dual bimodule $B$ with invariant form $\langle-,-\rangle_B$ the
   **induced form** on $BB_s$ is the unique invariant form satisfying, for all
   $b,b'\in B$,
   $$\langle\alpha(b),\alpha(b')\rangle=\partial_s(\langle b,b'\rangle_B),\qquad \langle\alpha(b),\beta(b')\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle_B=\langle\beta(b),\alpha(b')\rangle,\qquad \langle\beta(b),\beta(b')\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle_B\,\alpha_s,$$
   where $\alpha(b):=b\,c_{\mathrm{id}}$ and $\beta(b):=b\,c_s$;
4. the intersection form on a Bott-Samelson bimodule is non-degenerate as an
   $S$-valued form, and for a summand $B$ of a Bott-Samelson bimodule the
   restricted form is non-degenerate whenever $B$ has finite free right
   $S$-rank and the induced reduced form on $\overline B$ is non-degenerate
   (graded Nakayama);
5. the reduction of $\langle-,-\rangle$ is a graded symmetric $k$-valued form
   $\langle-,-\rangle_{\overline M}$ on $\overline M$
   ([[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]]), and for a
   finite right-free $M$ the $S$-valued form is non-degenerate if and only if
   the reduced form is graded non-degenerate;
6. Bott-Samelson bimodules and the indecomposable bimodules $B_w^R$ are
   self-dual, so
   $\dim(\overline{B_w^R})^{-i}=\dim(\overline{B_w^R})^{i}$ for all $i$
   (symmetric Betti numbers).

Additionally record the left/right asymmetry: the form is bilinear for the
right action and satisfies the two invariance identities displayed in (1); it is
not left $S$-bilinear in general, because $\langle rb,b'\rangle$ is defined
through the trace of a product while the two $S$-actions differ on
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$.
items.strategy: Items (1),(3) are direct computations in the commutative ring BS(x)(-m) and the multiplication rules c_id c_id = c_id, c_id c_s = c_s, c_s c_s = c_s alpha_s, using the identity Tr(chi_i gamma) = Tr_i(gamma); (2) is the induced-form calculation with the basis {alpha(e_i), beta(e_i)} and its dual; (4) is the determinant computation with the block matrix having identity diagonal blocks and the vanishing lower-left block (partial_s(1) = 0); (5) is the graded Nakayama lemma applied to the free right S-module together with the observation that an invariant form is the same as a bimodule map B -> DB. For (6), self-duality of Bott-Samelson bimodules follows from the explicit dual basis of the commutative presentation, and self-duality of B_w^R is a consequence of the base-change classification lemma proved on this page (the rational statement is part of the published type-A classification, and self-duality is preserved by the flat base change Q -> R).

items.title: Primitive subspaces, hard Lefschetz and the Hodge-Riemann signs: the dictionary of hypotheses S, hL and HR
items.statement:
**The linear-algebraic data.** Let $H=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}H^i$ be a
finite-dimensional graded real vector space, concentrated in a single parity
(all nonzero $H^i$ have $i\equiv j\pmod 2$ for one $j\in\{0,1\}$), equipped with
a graded symmetric bilinear form $\langle-,-\rangle$: symmetric in the sense of
[[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]] and graded in the sense
$\langle a,b\rangle=0$ unless $\deg a+\deg b=0$, non-degenerate in the sense that
the induced map $H\to H^*$ is an isomorphism; definiteness, inertia and
signature are used in the sense of
[[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]], and Sylvester's
law [[thm-sylvesters-law-of-inertia]] supplies the uniqueness of the inertia.
Let $L:H\to H$ be a **symmetric degree-two operator**, i.e. $L(H^i)\subseteq H^{i+2}$
and $\langle La,b\rangle=\langle a,Lb\rangle$ for all $a,b$.

**Hard Lefschetz.** The operator $L$ satisfies **hard Lefschetz** (hL) when
$$L^i:H^{-i}\longrightarrow H^i$$
is an isomorphism for every $i\ge0$. Define the **primitive subspaces**
$$P_L^{-i}:=\ker\bigl(L^{i+1}|_{H^{-i}}\bigr)\subseteq H^{-i}\qquad(i\ge0),$$
and the **Lefschetz forms**
$$(a,b)_L^{-i}:=\langle a,L^ib\rangle\qquad(a,b\in H^{-i},\ i\ge0).$$
Under hL the **primitive decomposition**
$$H=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}\bigoplus_{j=0}^{i}L^jP_L^{-i}$$
holds; it is proved in the primitive-decomposition lemma later on this page,
together with the non-degeneracy of the Lefschetz forms and the signature
formula for them.

**The Hodge-Riemann sign.** Assume $H\ne0$ and let $-d$ be its lowest nonzero
degree, so $H^{-d}\ne0$ and $H^i=0$ for $i<-d$. The **standard sign** at degree
$-i$ is $(-1)^{(d-i)/2}$; when $d-i$ is odd the primitive space $P_L^{-i}$ is
declared zero and the sign is not used. The pair $(H,L,\langle-,-\rangle)$
satisfies the **Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations with the standard sign**
(HR) when hL holds and the Lefschetz form $(a,b)_L^{-i}$ on $P_L^{-i}$ is
definite of sign $(-1)^{(d-i)/2}$ for every $i\ge0$, with the bottom space
$P_L^{-d}=H^{-d}$ positive definite. **HR with global sign** $\varepsilon\in\{\pm1\}$
means that the same statement holds with $(-1)^{(d-i)/2}$ replaced by
$\varepsilon(-1)^{(d-i)/2}$; the standard sign is thus the normalization that
makes the bottom form positive.

**The hypotheses S, hL, HR for Soergel bimodules.** For $x\in S_n$ let
$B_x^R$ be the indecomposable real Soergel bimodule with its reduced module
$\overline{B_x^R}$ ([[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]]).
The statement
$$\mathrm{S}(x):\qquad \operatorname{ch}(B_x^R)=\underline H_x$$
means that the character of $B_x^R$ is the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element
$\underline H_x$ in the Hecke algebra of the type-A page. On $\overline{B_x^R}$
use the centered grading, the operator
$$L:=\rho\cdot(-)$$
of left multiplication by a strictly dominant $\rho$ as in
[[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]], and the
**positively normalized intrinsic invariant form when $\mathrm{S}(x)$ holds**: the unique-up-to-scalar
non-degenerate invariant form of
[[def-invariant-intersection-form-on-a-bott-samelson-bimodule]], normalized so
that the bottom Lefschetz form $\langle\rho^{\ell(x)}c_{\mathrm{bot}},c_{\mathrm{bot}}\rangle$
on the one-dimensional space $\overline{B_x^R}^{-\ell(x)}$ equals $+1$. Here $d=\ell(x)$ by the proved normalized degree bounds. The property $\mathrm{hL}(x)$ always denotes hard Lefschetz for this operator on $\overline{B_x^R}$, independently of $\mathrm{S}(x)$. $\mathrm{HR}(x)$ denotes the conjunction of $\mathrm{S}(x)$ and the Hodge-Riemann relations with the standard sign for this normalized intrinsic form; its existence and uniqueness, and the nonzero positive bottom value used for normalization, are proved in [[lem-invariant-forms-on-soergel-bimodules-are-unique-up-to-scalar-and-nondegenerate]]. The **embedded-form statements**
refer to a reduced expression $\underline x$ of $x$ and an embedding
$B_x^R\subseteq\!\!\bigoplus\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$ as a direct summand: then
$\mathrm{HRbar}(x)$ requires the general Hodge-Riemann relations above for the restricted intersection form through every such embedding, and its equivalence with
$\mathrm{HR}(x)$ (the comparison scalar is positive) is the content of the
invariant-form uniqueness lemma later on this page. The strong embedded-form
statement $\mathrm{HRbar}(x)$ is formulated for the restricted forms and makes
sense without assuming $\mathrm{S}(x)$.

**The ascent and deformation packages.** Fix $xs>x$ and put
$M=B_x^RB_s^R$, whose reduced module has lowest degree $-\ell(x)-1$; the ascent
packages are read with
$$d=\ell(x)+1,\qquad L=L_0\ \text{or}\ L_\zeta,$$
and inherit hL, HR, HRbar, and the sign $(-1)^{(\ell(x)+1-i)/2}$ from the
general definition above, where $L_\zeta$ is the deformed Lefschetz operator
defined later on this page. Thus $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)$, $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)$ refer to
a fixed reduced-word induced form on $M$, while $\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)$ requires
the statement for every choice of reduced-word embeddings and induced forms;
the subscript $\zeta$ denotes the same statements for $L_\zeta$. The local
sign hypotheses $\mathrm{S}^\pm(y,x,s)$ concern the local intersection form
$(-,-)^{x,s}_y$ on $\operatorname{Hom}^0(B_y,M)$ defined later on this page:
$\mathrm{S}^+(y,x,s)$ means $(-1)^{(\ell(x)+1-\ell(y))/2}$-definiteness of that
form and $\mathrm{S}^-(y,x,s)$ the opposite definiteness, with the parity
convention of the primitive subspaces.

**Orthogonal sums.** If $H=\bigoplus_\alpha H_\alpha$ is an orthogonal direct
sum of $L$-stable graded subspaces and $H$ has lowest degree $-d$, then HR holds
for $(H,L,\langle-,-\rangle)$ if and only if each summand satisfies hL and its
primitive Lefschetz forms are definite with the **ambient** signs
$(-1)^{(d-i)/2}$; these need not be the summand's own standard signs when the
summands have different lowest degrees. The sign bookkeeping for orthogonal
blocks is used in the tensoring lemma of this page.
items.strategy: This fixes the centered grading and standard-sign normalization. The sign on primitives in degree -i is (-1)^{(d-i)/2}; it is positive at i=d and alternates every two degrees upward. For an indecomposable of length ell it equals (-1)^{(ell-i)/2}=(-1)^{(i-ell)/2}, precisely EW Theorem 1.4. For the tensor product in an ascent replace ell by ell(x)+1. The parity-only formula epsilon(-1)^{(-i+j)/2}, j=0 or 1, is equivalent after choosing epsilon to make the bottom form positive, and is not imposed simultaneously without that factor. Substantive primitive decomposition and form-normalization equivalences are proved by the named local lemmas. Orthogonal blocks use the common ambient signs; the tensoring lemma computes the necessary scalar signs explicitly.

items.title: Minimal complexes and the perverse truncations in the real type-A Soergel category
items.statement:
**The category and its radical.** Let $\mathcal B=\mathrm{SBim}_n^R$ be the real
graded type-A Soergel category of
[[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]], with degree-zero
morphisms; it is a graded additive idempotent-complete category
([[def-additive-category]], [[def-the-idempotent-completion-of-a-preadditive-category]])
whose objects are finite direct sums of shifts of the indecomposables $B_w^R$
([[lem-rational-and-real-type-a-soergel-characters-and-indecomposable-labels-agree]]).
Its **categorical radical** is the two-sided ideal
$$\operatorname{rad}\mathcal B:=\{f:M\to N\ :\ \text{for every }g:N\to M,\ 1_M-gf\text{ is invertible}\},$$
and $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B^{ss}:=\mathcal B/\operatorname{rad}\mathcal B$ is
the quotient functor. The radical is defined by the displayed invertibility
criterion and is not claimed to be nilpotent in general; on objects with local
endomorphism rings (as here, by the comparison lemma) it consists of the
non-units in the relevant endomorphism algebras.

**Minimal complexes.** Let $K^b(\mathcal B)$ be the homotopy category of bounded
cochain complexes of graded bimodules with degree-zero differentials
([[def-bounded-complex-of-graded-bimodules-and-signed-tensor-totalization]],
[[def-homotopy-category-of-chain-complexes]]). A bounded complex $F$ is
**minimal** when $q(d_F)=0$ in every degree, i.e. every differential of $F$
lies in the radical. Homological shifts are written $[j]$
([[def-shift-of-a-chain-complex]]); mapping cones are as in
[[def-mapping-cone-of-a-chain-map]]; contractibility and homotopies are as in
[[def-complex-homotopy-and-contractibility-in-an-additive-category]]; and the
two-term cancellation used on this page is
[[thm-homological-gaussian-elimination-splits-off-a-contractible-two-term-complex]]
with the block calculus of
[[def-invertible-differential-block-and-schur-complement-reduction]].

**Perverse bimodules.** Let $\underline H_x$ be the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of the
Hecke algebra of the frontier Hecke page, transported to this page by the
comparison lemma. A Soergel bimodule is **perverse** when its character is a
nonnegative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis elements
$\underline H_x$ (not of the standard basis elements $H_x$); it is
**p-split** when its indecomposable summands are shifts of perverse ones. Thus
if $\mathrm{S}(x)$ holds then $B_x^R$ is perverse, since its character is
$\underline H_x$; no other perversity of a normalized indecomposable is asserted
before $\mathrm{S}(x)$.

**The perverse cuts.** Let $M$ be p-split and fix a decomposition
$$M=\bigoplus_{x,k}B_x^R(k)^{m_{x,k}}$$
with the normalized $B_x^R$ perverse (such a decomposition exists by the
comparison lemma, and the cuts below are proved intrinsic by the structural
lemma). For $j\in\mathbb Z$ set
$$\tau_{\le j}M:=\bigoplus_{k\ge -j}B_x^R(k)^{m_{x,k}},\qquad \tau_{<j}M:=\tau_{\le j-1}M,\qquad \tau_{\ge j}M:=M/\tau_{<j}M,$$
and define the associated graded
$$H^j(M):=\bigl(\tau_{\le j}M/\tau_{<j}M\bigr)(j),$$
so that the $j$-th perverse piece is normalized by the internal shift $(j)$.
Internal shifts $(d)$ change module degrees and homological shifts $[j]$ change
complex degrees; the two are kept distinct throughout.

**The perverse subcategories of complexes.** For a bounded complex
$F=(F^i,d^i)$ define
$$F\in pK^b_{\ge0}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\ \text{is isomorphic in }K^b(\mathcal B)\ \text{to a complex with p-split terms and}\ \tau_{<-i}(F^i)=0\ \text{for all }i,$$
$$F\in pK^b_{\le0}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F\ \text{is isomorphic in }K^b(\mathcal B)\ \text{to a complex with p-split terms and}\ F^i=\tau_{\le-i}(F^i)\ \text{for all }i.$$
Equivalently, in the termwise decompositions the internal shifts $k$ satisfy
$k\le i$ for $pK^b_{\ge0}$ and $k\ge i$ for $pK^b_{\le0}$. The structural lemma
of this page supplies the semisimplicity of $\mathcal B^{ss}$, the existence and
uniqueness of minimal models, the intrinsicness and functoriality of the cuts,
their preservation under direct summands and their extension closure in
distinguished triangles; none of these properties is asserted by this
definition. The objects $pK^b_{\ge0}$ and $pK^b_{\le0}$ are the classes inside
which the Rouquier complexes of the next items are shown to lie, following the
orientation of Elias-Williamson Section 6.3.
items.strategy: Define the radical by the invertibility criterion and the minimal/perverse objects by the displayed conditions. The structural lemma proves their claimed well-definedness and model-independent properties; do not assert radical zero for a normalized indecomposable before S(x).

items.title: Invariant forms on an indecomposable Soergel bimodule are unique up to scalar, non-degenerate, and agree with the restricted Bott-Samelson form
items.strategy: Under S(x), the degree-zero Hom formula gives dim_R Hom^0(B_x,D B_x)=dim_R End^0(B_x)=1; this is not a rank-one assertion about Hom^bullet. Self-duality supplies an isomorphism B_x→D B_x, so each nonzero degree-zero invariant form is a nonzero real scalar multiple of a nondegenerate one. For a reduced-word embedding B_x→BS(x), the bottom degree is one-dimensional and maps isomorphically to the Bott-Samelson bottom degree. Its Lefschetz value is positive: expand rho^{ell(x)} on the bottom subexpression using the deleted-letter identity and induct on the length. Every reduced deletion has a positive coefficient (s_{i-1}...s_1rho)(alpha_{s_i}^vee) and positive top value by induction; nonreduced deletions contribute zero by degree bounds. Hence the restricted form is nonzero and its scalar comparison with the normalized intrinsic form is positive. This proves (1)-(3). For (4), S(z) and S(y) give Hom^0(B_z,D B_y)=0 for z≠y, so the isotypic components are orthogonal. On each component the invariant form is a real symmetric matrix on the multiplicity space tensored with the normalized form on B_z; if the total form is nondegenerate this matrix is nonsingular. Diagonalizing it gives an orthogonal sum of scalar copies. Definiteness of its sign is an additional HR input in the tensoring lemma, not an automatic consequence of nondegeneracy.

items.title: Hard Lefschetz gives the primitive decomposition, orthogonality and the signature formula
items.statement:
Let $H$ have a graded non-degenerate symmetric form and a symmetric degree-two operator $L$.

(a) If hL holds then $H=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}\bigoplus_{j=0}^{i}L^jP_L^{-i}$; more precisely, in each degree $-i$ one has $H^{-i}=\bigoplus_{k\ge0}L^kP_L^{-(i+2k)}$.

(b) In each degree $-i$, the decomposition of (a) is orthogonal for the Lefschetz form $\langle a,L^ib\rangle$.

(c) All Lefschetz forms on $H^{-i}$ are non-degenerate exactly when hL holds.

(d) If $H$ has one parity and lowest degree $-d$, standard HR is equivalent to hL together with the signature formula $\operatorname{sig}\bigl(\langle-,L^i-\rangle|_{H^{-i}}\bigr)=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^{(d-i-2k)/2}\dim P_L^{-(i+2k)}$ for every $i\ge0$ (zero spaces omitted).

(e) If $H$ satisfies hL, an $L$-stable graded subspace $V\subseteq H$ with $\dim V^{-i}=\dim V^i$ for all $i$ inherits hL; if $H$ satisfies HR then the restricted form on $V$ is non-degenerate and $V$ inherits the ambient primitive signs, and its standard global sign agrees with that of $H$ when their lowest degrees coincide.
items.strategy: Under hL, L^{i+2}:H^{-i-2}→H^{i+2} is invertible. For a∈H^{-i}, solve L^{i+2}b=L^{i+1}a and write a=(a-Lb)+Lb with the first term primitive. The intersection is zero by the same invertibility. Thus H^{-i}=P^{-i}⊕L H^{-i-2}; iteration and hL give the full primitive strings and dim P^{-i}=dim H^{-i}-dim H^{-i-2}. Symmetry of L makes this decomposition orthogonal: <p,L^{i+1}b>=<L^{i+1}p,b>=0. More generally the Lefschetz form on L^kP^{-(i+2k)} identifies with the primitive form <p,L^{i+2k}q>. Nondegeneracy of the original pairing identifies invertibility of L^i with nondegeneracy of its Lefschetz form. Taking signatures of those orthogonal pieces gives the displayed sum. Conversely descend from the bottom degree: subtract the already-determined lower primitive-string signatures to obtain the signature of each new primitive form. It equals plus or minus its full dimension; together with nondegeneracy this gives definiteness and the HR signs. For V, L^i is injective by inherited hL and is surjective by dimension symmetry. Apply the same primitive-decomposition construction inside V; its primitive spaces are V∩P_H^{-i} and the definite primitive forms restrict to them. Orthogonal primitive strings then give restricted nondegeneracy and ambient signs. This proves the stable-subspace assertion without assuming its primitive projectors preserve an arbitrary subspace in advance.

items.title: The deformed Lefschetz operator L_zeta on B_x B_s
items.statement:
**The operator.** Fix $x\in S_n$, a simple reflection $s$, a strictly dominant
$\rho\in S_2$ ([[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]])
and a real parameter $\zeta\ge0$. On the tensor product
$B_x^RB_s^R=B_x^R\otimes_SB_s^R$ define
$$L_\zeta:=(\rho\cdot(-))\otimes\mathrm{id}_{B_s^R}+\mathrm{id}_{B_x^R}\otimes(\zeta\,\rho\cdot(-)),$$
where the first summand is left multiplication by $\rho$ on the first factor and
the second summand is left multiplication by $\zeta\rho$ on the second factor.
Because the polynomial ring is commutative and the balanced tensor product
identifies $b r\otimes c=b\otimes rc$ for $r\in S$, the second summand equals
right multiplication by $\zeta\rho$ on the first factor; both summands are
degree-two, $S$-linear on the right, and commute, so $L_\zeta$ is a degree-two
right-$S$-linear endomorphism of $B_x^RB_s^R$. In particular $L_\zeta$ preserves
the submodule $MS_+$ for $M=B_x^RB_s^R$ and therefore descends to a degree-two
$\mathbb R$-linear endomorphism of the reduced module
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}$ ([[def-invariant-intersection-form-on-a-bott-samelson-bimodule]]
supplies the induced invariant form and the reduction conventions of
[[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]] apply).

**Symmetry.** Each summand of $L_\zeta$ is multiplication by an element in the
commutative position algebra of the tensor product: the first is multiplication
by $\rho$ on the first factor, the second is right (equivalently middle)
multiplication by $\zeta\rho$, which is self-adjoint for the induced invariant
form by the invariance identities of the form. Hence $L_\zeta$ is symmetric for
the induced form, and the Lefschetz forms $(\ ,\ )^{-i}_{L_\zeta}$ and the
primitive subspaces $P^{-i}_{L_\zeta}$ are those of
[[def-primitive-subspaces-hard-lefschetz-and-hodge-riemann-signs]] for this
operator.

**The deformation statements.** Write $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_\zeta$,
$\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_\zeta$ and $\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)_\zeta$ for centered hard
Lefschetz, the Hodge-Riemann relations and the strong embedded-form statement on
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}$ for the operator $L_\zeta$, with the bottom degree
$-\ell(x)-1$ and the standard sign
$(-1)^{(\ell(x)+1-i)/2}$ of the dictionary in
[[def-primitive-subspaces-hard-lefschetz-and-hodge-riemann-signs]]; the
definitions of $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_\zeta$ and $\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)_\zeta$ refer to
a fixed reduced-word induced form respectively to all choices of such forms.
At $\zeta=0$ the operator $L_0=\rho\cdot(-)\otimes\mathrm{id}$ is left
multiplication by $\rho$ on the first factor, so the zero-parameter statements
$\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_0$, $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_0$, $\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)_0$ are exactly
the undeformed statements $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)$, $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)$,
$\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)$ of the dictionary. For fixed data the family
$\zeta\mapsto L_\zeta$ is polynomial of degree one in $\zeta$.

**Summand stability.** Any direct summand $B\subseteq B_x^RB_s^R$ that is a
sub-bimodule is stable under $L_0$, because left multiplication by the central
element $\rho$ is a bimodule endomorphism; stability under $L_\zeta$ for
$\zeta>0$ is a separate condition, since a projector onto $B$ need not commute
with the middle-position operator. The undeformed summand implications used in
the induction of this page are supplied by the local restriction lemma later on
this page, after deforming the parameter back to $\zeta=0$; no statement of this
definition identifies a restricted positive-parameter operator with a
restriction of $L_\zeta$.
items.strategy: Check balancing: for b r⊗c=b⊗r c, both compositions with middle rho give b r⊗rho c=b⊗rho r c since the polynomial ring is commutative. All terms are right-linear, so preserve the right augmentation ideal. Invariance of the form proves symmetry separately for left multiplication on the first tensor factor and left multiplication on the second factor. The identities at zero and polynomial dependence are direct calculations. Do not infer hL(xs) or HR(xs) by restricting L_zeta to a chosen bimodule summand at positive zeta; use the separately proved undeformed restriction lemma.

items.title: Radical quotients, minimal complexes and perverse filtrations in the Soergel category
items.statement:
(1) The quotient $\mathcal B^{ss}$ is semisimple with simple classes $B_x(k)$ and endomorphism rings $\mathbb R$, and $q$ reflects isomorphisms.

(2) Every bounded complex of $\mathcal B$ has a minimal direct summand whose inclusion is a homotopy equivalence, and any two minimal models are isomorphic as complexes.

(3) Every direct summand of a perverse (respectively p-split) bimodule is perverse (respectively p-split).

(4) For perverse $M,N$ one has $\operatorname{Hom}(M,N(-i))=0$ for $i>0$.

(5) The perverse cuts on p-split bimodules are independent of the chosen decomposition and are preserved by every morphism.

(6) The definitions of $pK^b_{\ge0}$ and $pK^b_{\le0}$ can equivalently be tested on the minimal model, and both classes are closed under extensions in distinguished triangles.
items.strategy: Finite Krull-Schmidt decomposition and the base-change lemma give local finite-dimensional End^0(B_x(k)) with residue R. For a finite sum, quotient by its categorical radical is the product of matrix algebras over these residue fields, grouped by identical (x,k); all cross-class maps vanish there. The radical is nilpotent by the same finite-dimensional minimal-generator argument as in the base-change lemma. If q(f) is invertible, lift a two-sided inverse; the errors in the two compositions lie in these nilpotent radicals, so the finite geometric-series inverse proves f invertible. To minimize a bounded complex, if a differential survives q, isolate a nonzero matrix entry between identical simple classes, lift it to an invertible block, and apply Gaussian elimination. Each cancellation removes two indecomposable terms, so finitely many cancellations suffice. Between minimal models a homotopy equivalence becomes an ordinary degreewise isomorphism after q, since q-differentials are zero; isomorphism reflection gives an isomorphism of complexes. For perversity, a summand character has nonnegative standard-basis coefficients and is bar invariant. Since the total perverse character has no negative powers in that basis, each summand also has no negative powers. Its KL expansion, obtained by triangular subtraction, has coefficients in Z[v]; bar invariance forces each coefficient to be constant, and its constant equals the nonnegative constant of the standard coefficient, since the lower terms of each KL basis element are divisible by v. Thus summands are perverse. The p-split claim follows by indecomposable decomposition. The Hom formula on two constant KL expansions has no negative degrees, giving the asserted negative-shift vanishing. For shifted perverse objects, a map B_x(k)→B_y(l) can only exist if l-k≥0. Thus maps preserve the subobject defined by k≥-j; applying this to a change of decomposition and its inverse proves intrinsicness and functoriality of the cuts. A minimal model is obtained by removing pairs from a model; the cut bounds persist under direct summands. Finally, for a triangle F'→F→F''→ with F',F'' in either bound, choose representatives satisfying the termwise bounds and represent F by the cone of F''[-1]→F'. Its ith term is ^iF'⊕^iF'', which satisfies the same cut. This proves extension closure and supplies the preliminary properties used by the linearity and HR proofs.

items.title: Positive Rouquier complexes are Delta-split
items.statement:
Let $\underline x$ be a reduced expression for $x\in S_n$ and let $F_{\underline x}$ be the Rouquier complex $F_{s_1}\cdots F_{s_m}$ (or its minimal subcomplex). Then for every $y\in S_n$ there is an isomorphism in the homotopy category of graded bimodules
$$\Gamma_{\ge y}(F_{\underline x})/\Gamma_{>y}(F_{\underline x})\;\cong\;\begin{cases}\Delta_x,&y=x,\\0,&y\ne x,\end{cases}$$
where $\Delta_x=R_x(-\ell(x))$. Equivalently: the Bruhat support subquotient of a positive Rouquier complex is contractible except in the top layer $\Delta_x$; $F_{\underline x}$ is $\Delta$-split in the sense that each of its support subquotients is a direct sum of standard bimodules, and the top layer is a single $\Delta_x$. No positivity of characters and no assumption $\mathrm{S}$ is used; the statement is unconditional for every finite type-$A$ Coxeter group and the coordinate reflection realization.
items.strategy: Prove the nabla statement for inverse complexes E_x first and dualize to the displayed Delta statement for F_x, following LW Proposition 3.7, with all required support commutation justified locally. Choose a Bruhat-compatible enumeration in pairs w_{2j},w_{2j+1}=w_{2j}s by enumerating W/<s> and refining each pair. Only finitely many pairs in the current support enter the induction. Each paired prefix A is s-stable. Its support cut Gamma_A M and the quotient have finite standard flags and hence are free as right polynomial modules (split each flag successively). Tensoring Gamma_A M→M with B_s remains injective. Over the fraction field, tensoring with B_s only sends graph labels w to {w,ws}. Thus the resulting submodule is supported in A and the quotient in its complement, because A is s-stable. The quotient is right-free: its standard flag tensors into rank-one/two graph flags, each right-free. Consequently any A-supported element of that quotient vanishes after fraction-field localization and is zero; this proves Gamma_A(MB_s)=(Gamma_A M)B_s. Exactness of tensoring and quotienting gives the same isomorphism for a two-element paired subquotient and hence for tensoring with E_s. This is the commutativity isomorphism of LW (17), now with a local argument rather than importing Williamson Proposition 6.5. The length-zero/one complexes are checked by the explicit rank-one maps. Write x=zs with ell(z)=ell(x)-1. By induction the paired subquotient over {z,x} of E_z is R_z(ell(z)); tensoring E_s gives the two-term rank-one graph-union complex whose two single-graph subquotients are the identity complex at z and R_x(ell(x)) in degree zero at x. For a different pair {y,ys}, both single-layer complexes of E_z are contractible by induction. Their extension splits after restriction to (R,R^s): the two graph modules have identical invariant-right action r↦y(r), and a standard-free extension is left-free and annihilated by the common graph ideal (after fraction-field localization, then by torsion-freeness). Thus a left-module splitting is invariant-right-linear. Tensoring B_s gives a termwise split short exact sequence of complexes and hence a triangle with contractible outer terms; the paired B_s product is contractible. The triangle E_z(-1)→E_zB_s→E_zE_s and the zero single-layer factors then show both corresponding layers of E_x vanish. The two support cuts commute with passing to the paired quotient, so these cover every layer. Right/left duality converts nabla cuts to Delta cuts and E_x to F_x, giving the stated Delta-split property. Only rank-one graph calculations, finite support flags, tensor exactness and Gaussian cancellation are used; no character conjecture or positivity theorem is assumed.

items.title: Signature constancy in a Lefschetz family, the L-stable subspace lemma and the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement:
(1) **Family lemma.** Let $L_t$, $t\in[a,b]$, be a continuous family of symmetric degree-two operators on $H$, each satisfying hL, and suppose $L_{t_0}$ satisfies HR with the standard sign for one $t_0\in[a,b]$. Then every $L_t$ satisfies HR with the standard sign; in the application the family is $L_\zeta$, $\zeta\ge0$, which is polynomial (hence continuous) in $\zeta$.

(2) **Weak-Lefschetz substitute.** Let $\varphi:V\to W(1)$ be a map of graded $R[L]$-modules such that (a) $\varphi$ is injective in degrees $\le-1$, (b) $V,W$ carry graded forms with $\langle\varphi(a),\varphi(b)\rangle_W=\langle a,Lb\rangle_V$, and (c) $W$ satisfies HR with the standard sign. Then $L^i:V^{-i}\to V^i$ is injective for all $i\ge0$, and if $\dim V^i=\dim V^{-i}$ for all $i$ then $L$ satisfies hL on $V$.

(3) **Sign bookkeeping.** If in (2) the lowest degree of $W$ is $-\ell$ and of $V$ is $-(\ell+1)$, then the Lefschetz form on $V^{-(\ell+1)}$ is $\pm$definite with the same sign as on $W^{-\ell}$, so if $V$ satisfies HR with the standard sign then $V$ has the standard sign if and only if $W$ does.

(4) **Degenerate shifted case.** Let the form on $H$ not be assumed non-degenerate and suppose $L^i:H^{-d-i}\to H^{-d+i}$ is an isomorphism for all $i\ge0$ with $d$ a positive integer. Then the Lefschetz form $(h,h')_L^{-i}=\langle h,L^ih'\rangle$ on $H^{-i}$ is identically zero for every $i\ge0$.

(5) **Stable-subspace lemma.** If $(H,L,\langle-,-\rangle)$ satisfies hL and HR and $V\subseteq H$ is an $L$-stable graded subspace with $\dim V^{-i}=\dim V^i$ for all $i$, then the restricted operator and form satisfy hL and HR on $V$ with the ambient degree-by-degree signs; the restricted form is non-degenerate, and its standard global sign agrees with the ambient standard sign if the lowest nonzero degrees agree.
items.strategy: (1) is the constancy of the signature on the open set of non-degenerate symmetric matrices along a continuous path: the eigenvalues of a continuous family of symmetric matrices depend continuously on the parameter, so the numbers of positive and negative eigenvalues are locally constant, hence constant on the connected interval. (2) elementary: for 0 != a in V^{-i} with i >= 1, phi(a) is non-zero by injectivity in degrees <= -1; if L^i phi(a) = phi(L^i a) != 0 then L^i a != 0; otherwise phi(a) is primitive and <phi(a),phi(a)>^{-i+1}_L = <a, L^i a>_V is non-zero with a definite sign by the HR relations of W. (3) inspect the lowest-degree case of the same computation. (4) use the shifted primitive decomposition H^m = \oplus_j L^j Q^{m-2j} with Q^{-d-i}_L := ker(L^{i+1}) \subset H^{-d-i} and show <L^j x, L^k y> = <x, L^{j+k-m} y> = 0 because the exponent j+k-m is at least the defining exponent of the primitive condition and d > 0. For (5), inherited injectivity of L^i and symmetry of the dimensions prove hL on V. Its primitive subspaces ker L^{i+1}∩V^{-i} lie in those of H and inherit definite Lefschetz forms. The primitive decomposition of V follows from hL. Orthogonality of primitive strings and the definite primitive forms show that the restricted graded form is nondegenerate and give the asserted signs. Equal lowest degrees give the same standard global sign. In (3) do not assume the conclusion in advance: the computation shows that whenever V satisfies HR (with either global sign), its standard-sign normalization is equivalent to that of W.

items.title: The local intersection form on Hom(B_y, B_x B_s)
items.statement:
**The setting.** Fix $x\in S_n$, a simple reflection $s$ with $xs>x$, and
$y<xs$ in the Bruhat order; assume $\mathrm{S}(z)$ for all $z<xs$. Choose
reduced-word embeddings $B_y^R\subseteq\!\!\bigoplus\mathrm{BS}(\underline y)$
and $B_x^R\subseteq\!\!\bigoplus\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$, and equip $B_y^R$,
$B_x^R$ with the positively normalized non-degenerate invariant forms obtained
by restriction, so that the bottom Lefschetz values are $+1$; equip
$M:=B_x^RB_s^R$ with the induced invariant form of
[[def-invariant-intersection-form-on-a-bott-samelson-bimodule]]. Under
$\mathrm{S}(y)$ and $\mathrm{S}(x)$ these forms exist and are unique up to
positive scalars, and the choices enter only through positive factors
([[lem-invariant-forms-on-soergel-bimodules-are-unique-up-to-scalar-and-nondegenerate]]).

**The local intersection form.** Let
$$E_y:=\operatorname{Hom}^0(B_y^R,M)$$
be the finite-dimensional real space of degree-zero bimodule maps. For
$f,g\in E_y$ define the **local intersection form**
$$(f,g)^{x,s}_y:=g^*\circ f\ \in\ \operatorname{End}^0(B_y^R)=\mathbb R,$$
where $g^*:M\to B_y^R$ is the **adjoint** of $g$ with respect to the two
non-degenerate forms, uniquely characterized by
$\langle g(b),m\rangle_M=\langle b,g^*(m)\rangle_{B_y}$ for all $b\in B_y^R$,
$m\in M$; adjunction is the standard transpose operation of
[[def-transpose-of-a-linear-map]] under the identifications
$B_y^R\to (B_y^R)^*$ and $M\to M^*$ induced by the forms
([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]). The adjoint construction
identifies $\operatorname{Hom}^0(B_y^R,M)$ with
$\operatorname{Hom}^0(M,B_y^R)$.

**Basic properties.** The form $(-,-)^{x,s}_y$ is symmetric: the adjoint of
$g^*f$ is $f^*g$, and a scalar endomorphism of $B_y^R$ is self-adjoint for its
invariant form. It is $\mathbb R$-bilinear, and it changes only by a positive
scalar when the chosen normalized forms or reduced-word embeddings are varied:
scaling the form on $M$ by $a>0$ and the form on $B_y^R$ by $b>0$ scales
$(-,-)^{x,s}_y$ by $a/b$, and the invariant-form uniqueness lemma shows that any
two choices compare by positive scalars. Define
$$\mathrm{S}^\pm(y,x,s)$$
to mean that $(-,-)^{x,s}_y$ is definite of sign
$(-1)^{(\ell(x)+1-\ell(y))/2}$, respectively its negative, with the parity
convention of
[[def-primitive-subspaces-hard-lefschetz-and-hodge-riemann-signs]]: when the
numerator is odd the corresponding primitive space is zero and the sign
condition is not used.

**Status.** The definition uses degree-zero Hom throughout; no statement
identifies the rank of the full graded Hom module with a Kazhdan-Lusztig
multiplication coefficient. The dimension of $E_y$ in terms of the
multiplication formula, and the equivalence of non-degeneracy of these forms
with the actual summand multiplicities of $M$, are proved in the detection
theorem later on this page; they are not part of this definition.
items.strategy: The nondegenerate graded invariant forms identify each bimodule with its dual, so adjoints are well-defined degree-zero bimodule maps. Under S(y), End^0(B_y)=R, giving the scalar-valued composition. The adjoint of g* f is f* g, and a scalar endomorphism is self-adjoint, so the form is symmetric. Scaling the M-form by a positive scalar a and the B_y-form by a positive scalar b scales this form by a/b. The invariant-form uniqueness lemma ensures these comparisons are positive for all chosen reduced-word embeddings. The definition uses degree-zero Hom throughout; its quantitative detection properties have a separate proved supplier.

items.title: Tensoring a direct sum of Hodge-Riemann bimodules with B_s preserves the signs
items.statement: Fix $\zeta\ge0$ and a self-dual Soergel bimodule $B=\bigoplus_zB_z^{R,m_z}$ such that $m_z\ne0$ implies $\mathrm{S}(z)$ and $\mathrm{HR}(z,s)_\zeta$; if $\zeta=0$ assume in addition that $m_z=0$ whenever $zs<z$. Assume $B$ is even or odd, carries an invariant non-degenerate form and satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to left multiplication by $\rho$. Then $BB_s$ satisfies HR with the standard sign with respect to $L_\zeta$ and the induced form. More precisely, if the lowest degree of $B$ is $-d$, then the restriction of its form to a $B_z$ summand is $(-1)^{(d-\ell(z))/2}$ times a positive multiple of the normalized form on $B_z$. Tensoring gives the primitive sign $(-1)^{(d+1-i)/2}$ on degree $-i$ of $BB_s$, whose lowest degree is $-d-1$.
items.strategy: Under S(z), the degree-zero Hom formula gives Hom^0(B_z,D B_y)=0 for z≠y and End^0(B_z)=R, so the isotypic decomposition is orthogonal and its invariant forms are scalar matrices on the multiplicity spaces. If the lowest degree of B is -d, the bottom space of each B_z summand (degree -ell(z)) is primitive for rho. HR on B says that the induced multiplicity-space Lefschetz form has sign (-1)^{(d-ell(z))/2}. Choose an orthogonal basis in that definite space and use End^0(B_z)=R to obtain orthogonal indecomposable copies; their restricted invariant forms are that sign times positive multiples of the normalized intersection form. The induced tensor-product forms preserve this orthogonal decomposition into B_zB_s blocks, and L_zeta preserves these blocks because the projections on B commute with its left and right actions. On a primitive vector of degree -i, HR(z,s)_zeta gives sign (-1)^{(ell(z)+1-i)/2}; multiplying by the form scalar gives (-1)^{(d+1-i)/2}. This is precisely the common standard HR sign for BB_s. At zero the hypotheses exclude descent summands, so the proof never assumes HR for a shifted descent block; the degenerate-shift analysis is used separately in the zero-parameter hard-Lefschetz theorem.

items.title: Right-descent Soergel bimodules descend to simple invariants under the character hypothesis
items.statement:
Let $M=B_x^R$ over $S$ and let $s$ be a right descent, $xs<x$. Assume $\mathrm{S}(x)$. Then there is a graded $(S,S^s)$-bimodule $N$ and an isomorphism $M\cong N\otimes_{S^s}S$. Consequently $MB_s=M(1)\oplus M(-1)$; choosing the decomposition $S=S^s\oplus(\alpha_s/2)S^s$ in the middle tensor factor, the reduced operator $L_\zeta$ has, with respect to the resulting identification $MB_s=M(1)\oplus M(-1)$, the matrix
$$L_\zeta=\begin{pmatrix}\rho\cdot(-)&0\\ \zeta\rho(\alpha_s^\vee)&\rho\cdot(-)\end{pmatrix},$$
where the scalar off-diagonal entry is a degree-two map $M(1)\to M(-1)$. The construction requires no singular-category classification or character conjecture beyond $\mathrm{S}(x)$. If $\mathrm{hL}(x)$ also holds and $\zeta>0$, this matrix satisfies centered hard Lefschetz; at $\zeta=0$ it fails centered hard Lefschetz.
items.strategy: The comparison/classification lemma supplies M B_s=M(1)⊕M(-1), End^0(M)=R and the one-dimensional bottom degree M^{-ell(x)}. Write U=M⊗_{R^s}R, so M B_s=U(1). The multiplication counit c:U→M, c(b⊗r)=br, is nonzero on the lowest degree (b⊗1↦b). In U=M⊕M(-2), that lowest degree belongs only to M. Hence the restriction of c to the first summand is a nonzero scalar endomorphism and is invertible. Rescale its inclusion to obtain a graded bimodule section σ:M→U with cσ=id. The twisted counit c_s:U→M_s, c_s(b⊗r)=b s(r), is balanced over R^s and left-linear; its right action is twisted by s. Set t=c_sσ. As a map on the underlying space t is right-s-semilinear, left-linear and degree zero. On the one-dimensional bottom degree σ(b)=b⊗1, so t(b)=b. Therefore t² is an ordinary degree-zero bimodule endomorphism, scalar because End^0(M)=R, with scalar 1 on the bottom degree; hence t²=id. Since s(r)-r is divisible by alpha_s, c_s(u)-c(u) belongs to M alpha_s for every u, and consequently t(m)-m belongs to M alpha_s. Put N={m:t(m)=m}. Every m splits into invariant and anti-invariant parts (m±t(m))/2. An anti-invariant m equals n alpha_s because it is divisible by alpha_s. Right freeness makes alpha_s multiplication injective; t(m)=-m and s(alpha_s)=-alpha_s then imply t(n)=n. Thus M=N⊕N alpha_s as an (R,R^s)-bimodule and multiplication gives N⊗_{R^s}R≅M. This proves the necessary descent seam locally. Compute the operator matrix using inclusion iota_1(r)=r, iota_2(r)=alpha_s r/2 and projections pi_1(r)=(r+s(r))/2, pi_2(r)=∂_s r. They satisfy pi_a iota_b=δ_ab. Multiplication by rho in the middle factor has entries pi_1(rho), pi_1(alpha_s rho)/2, rho(alpha_s^vee), ∂_s(alpha_s rho)/2. All entries except the constant bottom-left entry have positive polynomial degree and become zero as right multiplications on the reduced module. Left rho contributes the same diagonal operator on both shifts. This gives the claimed matrix. Under hL(x), decompose Mbar into centered primitive rho strings. Normalize the nonzero off-diagonal scalar to 1, and on a string u_0,...,u_m of degrees -m,-m+2,...,m let v_-,v_+ have degrees -1,+1. The matrix operator e satisfies e^k(u_j v_-)=u_{j+k}v_-+k u_{j+k-1}v_+ and e^k(u_jv_+)=u_{j+k}v_+, with out-of-range indices zero. In degree -k with 0≤k≤m-1 and k congruent to m+1 modulo 2, a source basis is u_jv_-,u_{j-1}v_+ for j=(m+1-k)/2; the corresponding target basis gives matrix [[1,0],[k,1]], invertible. At the extreme k=m+1 the map sends u_0v_- to (m+1)u_mv_+, nonzero. All other relevant pieces are zero. This proves hL for each two-shift string and hence for their direct sum, without importing sl_2 semisimplicity. At zero the bottom vector of M(1) in degree -ell(x)-1 is killed by rho^{ell(x)+1}, proving failure.

items.strategy: Use Corollary 6.7 (F_x in pK^b_{>=0}, proved by induction on ell(x) from the two lemmas 6.5 and 6.6: for xs < x, B_xF_s = B_x(-1) via the rank-one splitting and contractions; for xs > x, B_xF_s lies in pK^b_{>=0} because the KL multiplication formula and S on the relevant labels give an unshifted lower-summand decomposition and hence perversity in the KL basis) and Lemma 6.11: if ^iF_x contains a summand B_z(j) with z < x, then ^{i-1}F_x contains a summand B_{z'}(j') with z' > z and j' < j. The argument applies Gamma_{>=z/>z} to F_x, uses the Delta-splitness theorem to split the resulting complex, and tracks the summand Delta_z(j): it cannot survive in cohomology, cannot be hit from degree i+1 for degree reasons, and hence is hit from degree i-1, forcing z' > z and j' < j. From Lemma 6.11, ^0F_x has only summands B_x, hence equals B_x (using Gamma_{>=x/>x}); induction gives tau_{>-i}(^iF_x) = 0, i.e. F_x in pK^b_{<=0}. The parity statement is the standard induction on the length filtration: the summands of B_sB_z with sz > z are B_{sz} plus terms B_v with v < z and v of parity opposite to z, so the shift parity propagates as stated. This is the conditional 'linearity' theorem inside the simultaneous induction; no circular appeal to the Soergel theorem is made.

items.title: Undeformed Lefschetz and Hodge-Riemann restrict to the next Soergel summand
items.statement:
Let $xs>x$. The normalized indecomposable $B_{xs}^R$ occurs as a bimodule summand of $B_x^RB_s^R$.

(a) If $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_0$ holds, then $\mathrm{hL}(xs)$ holds.

(b) If $\mathrm{S}(<xs)$ and $\mathrm{hL}(y)$ for every $y<xs$ hold, then $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_0$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{hL}(xs)$.

(c) If $\mathrm{HRbar}(x,s)_0$ holds, then the restriction to the chosen $B_{xs}^R$ summand satisfies the Hodge-Riemann relations for its induced form; once $\mathrm{S}(xs)$ has been established, positive comparison of invariant forms gives $\mathrm{HR}(xs)$ and $\mathrm{HRbar}(xs)$ with the standard sign.

(d) More generally an $L_0$-stable graded subspace with symmetric Betti numbers inherits HR with the ambient signs, and an $L_0$-stable graded direct summand inherits hL. These conclusions apply to a positive deformation only if the chosen subspace, and for the direct-sum argument its complement, are preserved by that operator; they make no identification of the restricted positive operator with left multiplication by $\rho$.
items.strategy: For hL, the inclusion and projection of any bimodule summand commute with left multiplication rho=L_0 and remain split after right reduction. The map L_0^i is block diagonal on the reduced direct sum. If it is invertible, each diagonal block is invertible; in particular its B_xs block is rho^i. Under S(<xs), the comparison/classification lemma gives an unshifted decomposition B_xB_s=B_xs⊕⊕B_y^{a_y}. Hence hL(xs) and hL(y) for lower y make every block invertible, proving the converse. For HR, the reduced B_xs has symmetric Betti numbers by self-duality. Apply the stable-subspace lemma: injectivity of rho^i inherited from the ambient hL plus dimension symmetry gives hL on B_xs; its primitive spaces are intersections with ambient primitive spaces and inherit definite forms. Primitive decomposition proves restricted nondegeneracy. The lowest degrees of B_xs and B_xB_s are both -ell(xs), so the signs and positive normalization agree. For every embedding B_xs→BS(xs), use the multiplicity-one top summand and its positive lowest-degree Lefschetz value to compare restrictions; after S(xs), uniqueness of invariant forms gives a positive scalar comparison with its normalized intersection form. This gives the strong embedded-form formulation and HR(xs). No claim uses stability of an arbitrary bimodule summand under L_zeta for zeta>0.

items.title: Non-degeneracy of the local intersection forms detects Soergel's conjecture one step higher
items.statement:
Fix $x,s$ with $xs>x$ and assume $\mathrm{S}(y)$ for every $y<xs$. Put $M=B_x^RB_s^R$ and write the Kazhdan-Lusztig multiplication formula $\underline H_x\underline H_s=\underline H_{xs}+\sum_{y<xs}\mu_y\underline H_y$ with integer constants $\mu_y$. For each $y<xs$ let $E_y=\operatorname{Hom}^0(B_y^R,M)$ carry the local intersection form of [[def-local-intersection-form-for-a-soergel-summand]]. Then:

(1) $\dim_{\mathbb R}E_y=\mu_y$, while the full graded Hom module has graded rank $\langle\underline H_y,\underline H_x\underline H_s\rangle$, generally not $\mu_y$;

(2) the following are equivalent: $\mathrm{S}(xs)$; non-degeneracy of every local intersection form on $E_y$, $y<xs$; perfection of every degree-zero composition pairing $E_y\times\operatorname{Hom}^0(M,B_y^R)\to\operatorname{End}^0(B_y^R)=\mathbb R$; and equality of the actual multiplicity $a_y$ of $B_y^R$ in $M$ with $\mu_y$ for every $y<xs$.

The unconditional top summand is $B_{xs}$ with multiplicity one, and under $\mathrm{S}(<xs)$ all remaining summands are unshifted $B_y^R$. No positivity of Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials or conjecture at $xs$ is assumed.
items.strategy: Use the comparison/classification lemma to write M=B_xs⊕⊕B_y^{a_y} with no shifts. Under S(<xs), the Hom formula computes the graded rank of Hom^bullet(B_y,M) as (H_y,H_xH_s). All powers in that polynomial are nonnegative and its constant term is μ_y because (H_y,H_z) has constant term δ_yz for KL basis elements. Polynomial scalars have nonnegative degree, so the dimension of the degree-zero Hom space is precisely that constant term. For the composition pairing, a composite between B_y and a different indecomposable summand cannot be a nonzero scalar: otherwise rescaling gives a retraction and forces that indecomposable to be B_y. Thus only the a_y identical summands contribute. Their scalar-coordinate pairing is the usual evaluation pairing of rank a_y; the adjoint identification with E_y preserves this rank even if the chosen splitting is not orthogonal. Therefore the local intersection form is nondegenerate exactly when a_y=dim E_y=μ_y. Character additivity gives ch(B_xs)=H_xs+Σ(μ_y-a_y)H_y. Independence of the KL basis proves that these multiplicity equalities are equivalent to S(xs). This supplies both directions of Soergel's omnibus lemma locally.

items.title: Hodge-Riemann relations hold for large positive deformation, and the deformation principle
items.statement:
Let $B$ be a Soergel bimodule satisfying hL and HR with the standard sign. Then for $\zeta\gg0$ the induced operator $L_\zeta$ on $BB_s$ satisfies hL and HR with the standard sign (Theorem 5.1).

The proof contains the following **signature comparison** (Lemma 5.2): if $V,W$ are finite-dimensional graded spaces with graded non-degenerate forms and Lefschetz operators satisfying hL, $W$ is even or odd, $\dim V=(v+v^{-1})\dim W$, and $W$ satisfies HR with the standard sign, then $V$ satisfies HR with the standard sign if and only if for all $i\ge0$ the signature of the Lefschetz form on the primitive subspace $P_W^{-i+1}$ equals the signature of the Lefschetz form on all of $V^{-i}$.

Consequently (Corollary 5.3): if $\mathrm{HR}(x)$ holds and $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds for every $\zeta\ge0$, then $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds for every $\zeta\ge0$; more generally, if $\mathrm{hL}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds for all $\zeta\ge0$ and $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds for a single $\zeta_0\ge0$, then $\mathrm{HR}(x,s)_\zeta$ holds for all $\zeta\ge0$. In the signature comparison use the convention $P_W^1=0$; no positive-degree primitive space is introduced.
items.strategy: Use induced-form pairings on B (no product pq inside B). Hyperbolic-block congruence leaves Q_zeta=Q_0+zeta*i*rho(alpha_s^vee)*Q for i>0, while i=0 has an empty Q block and zero signature. Finitely many nonzero degrees give one large-parameter bound. Telescoping primitive dimensions proves both directions of the signature comparison; continuous nondegenerate families prove deformation.

items.title: Embedding theorem: local intersection forms are isometric to primitive Lefschetz forms
items.strategy: Write M=B_xB_s, ell=ell(y), and use the exact Delta-flag sequence 0→Delta_y=Gamma_{≥y}B_y→B_y→Q→0. Under S(y), ch(Q)=underline H_y-H_y lies in vZ_{≥0}[v] on the standard basis, because it consists of the actual lower support layers of B_y. Also ch(M)=underline H_x underline H_s has nonnegative standard coefficients from its actual support flag. The Hom formula and graded freeness give an exact sequence 0→Hom^bullet(Q,M)→Hom^bullet(B_y,M)→Hom^bullet(Delta_y,M)→0: left exactness identifies the kernel, and the graded Hom formula gives additive graded ranks for all three free modules. Their graded Hilbert series are those ranks times the same polynomial-ring Hilbert series. Hence the image has exactly the Hilbert series of the target in every degree, proving surjectivity (a mere ungraded rank comparison would not suffice). In degrees ≤0 the first module vanishes; hence degree-zero restriction is an isomorphism Hom^0(B_y,M)→Hom^0(Delta_y,M), while no full graded isomorphism is asserted. Hom(Delta_y,M) identifies with Gamma_yM shifted by ell, and the same degree bound makes Gamma_yM supported in degrees ≥ell. The support-layer inclusion is a right-module summand by the finite support-filtration/localization supplier; thus reduction injects its degree-ell part into Mbar^ell (if a vector belongs to Gamma_yM∩M R_+, project to that summand to put it in Gamma_yM R_+, whose degree-ell part is zero). A generator c of Delta_y maps to a nonzero generator of B_ybar^ell; evaluation at c therefore injects degree-zero Hom into Mbar^ell. Since HR(y) gives hL(y), rho^ell c_bot is a nonzero scalar multiple of c after reduction. If f(c_bot) vanished then f(rho^ell c_bot) would vanish, contradicting that injection. This proves injectivity of bottom evaluation. The reduced B_y is supported in [-ell,ell], so rho^{ell+1} annihilates c_bot after reduction, and bimodule linearity puts the image in P^{-ell}. For the isometry, g* f is the local scalar, so N(f,g)=<g* f(c_bot),rho^ell c_bot>_{B_y}=<f(c_bot),rho^ell g(c_bot)>_M, with N>0 by the normalized HR(y) form. Definite primitive forms restrict to definite forms on these images; the detection theorem then gives S(xs).

items.title: Minimal positive Rouquier complexes carry the induced Hodge-Riemann signs
items.statement: Assume $\mathrm S(\le x)$ and $\mathrm{HR}(y,s)$ for every $y<x$ and simple $s$ with $ys>y$. Fix a reduced expression $\underline x$ of $x$. Then $F_x$ satisfies the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations in the following sense: there exists an embedding as a direct summand $F_x\subseteq^{\oplus}F_{s_1}\cdots F_{s_m}$ such that for every tuple $\lambda=(\lambda_{x'})_{x'\in\pi(x,j)}$ of strictly positive real numbers and every $j\ge0$, the space $^jF_x(-j)$ embedded in $\bigoplus_{x'\in\pi(x,j)}\mathrm{BS}(x')$ carries the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations with respect to the rescaled form $\langle-,-\rangle_\lambda$ and the Lefschetz operator given by left multiplication by $\rho$, with the global sign fixed so that the Lefschetz form is positive definite on the primitive subspaces in degrees congruent to $-m+j\pmod4$. Here $\pi(x,j)$ is the set of subexpressions of $\underline x$ obtained by deleting $j$ letters and $^jF_x(-j)\subseteq^{\oplus}\bigoplus_{x'\in\pi(x,j)}\mathrm{BS}(x')$ is the canonical summand inclusion of [F1]. The existence of such an embedding and all its sign conclusions hold for every reduced expression; no scalar comparison of the entire multiplicity-space forms from different expressions is required.
items.strategy: Induct on the Bruhat order as in the proof of Proposition 6.13. Write x = ys and use the last letter s. The inductive hypothesis gives an embedding of F_y with the HR property for every tuple of positive scalars; the complex F_x is a summand of F_yF_s, so jF_x(-j) is a summand of jF_yB_s(-j) \oplus j-1F_y(-j+1). Decompose jF_y(-j) = B_up \oplus B_down according to whether zs > z or zs < z. Under S, the canonical decomposition into isotypic components V_z \otimes B_z is available; B_upB_s is perverse and B_downB_s = B_down(1) \oplus B_down(-1); the change of decomposition is not orthogonal but the restriction of the Lefschetz form to B_down(1) vanishes by the degenerate shifted Lemma 2.5, and the projection of jF_x(-j) to B_downB_s lands in B_down(1) by the perversity of F_x, so that projection contributes nothing to the form. The remaining map jF_x(-j) -> B_upB_s \oplus j-1F_y(-j+1) is an isometry, and it is injective because applying the quotient functor q gives a split inclusion (a map from perverse degree 0 to perverse degree -1 vanishes after q). The codomain satisfies HR with the required global signs: j-1F_y(-j+1) by induction, and B_upB_s by the tensoring lemma applied to each summand B_z with zs > z; then the target is an orthogonal sum of HR spaces with matching signs, and the source is a rho-stable summand with symmetric Betti numbers, so Lemma 2.2 gives HR for the source. Proposition 6.12 (the tensoring lemma) is applied exactly to the summands of B_up.

items.title: The minimal Rouquier differential supplies the injectivity input of the weak-Lefschetz substitute
items.statement:
(1) **Right-module retraction.** For every $x$ and every reduced expression of $x$, the minimal Rouquier complex $F_x$ is homotopy equivalent, as a complex of graded right $S$-modules, to the single right module $S(-\ell(x))$ concentrated in cohomological degree $0$. Consequently the right reduction has $H^0(\overline{F_x})\cong\mathbb R(-\ell(x))$, one copy of $\mathbb R$ in internal degree $\ell(x)$, and $H^j(\overline{F_x})=0$ for $j\ne0$.

(2) **Injectivity criterion.** Let $C$ be a bounded below complex of graded free right $S$-modules with $C^{-1}=0$ whose right reduction satisfies $H^{-1}(\overline C)=0$ and whose $H^0(\overline C)$ is concentrated in a single internal degree $d$. Then the reduced first differential $\overline{d^0}:\overline{C^0}\to\overline{C^1}$ is injective in every internal degree $\ne d$; in particular it is injective in internal degrees $\le d-1$. The conclusion is unchanged if $C$ is replaced by a homotopy-equivalent complex $C'$ with $C'^{-1}=0$ obtained by cancelling contractible two-term summands whose source lies in a positive cohomological degree, in particular the contractible shifted-descent summands occurring in the zero-parameter hard-Lefschetz theorem.

(3) **Application to the ascent differential.** Let $xs>x$ and assume $\mathrm S(\le x)$. Then the first differential of the complex $F_xF_s$, whose source is $B_x^RB_s^R$ and whose target is $^1F_xB_s\oplus B_x^R(1)$, has reduced form injective in internal degrees $\le\ell(x)$. The complex $F_xF_s$ need not itself be minimal, and no minimality is used in the conclusion.

(4) **Separation of inputs.** The form compatibility $\langle b,L_\zeta b'\rangle=\langle\varphi b,\varphi b'\rangle_\gamma$ and the operator commutation $\varphi(L_\zeta b)=L\varphi(b)$ used in the hard-Lefschetz proof are independent additional inputs that must be verified separately using the deleted-word factorization and the induced forms; in the zero-parameter descent case the form on the shifted descent piece vanishes and the hard-Lefschetz argument must separate the kernel of $d_3$ rather than apply the criterion of (2) to the whole target.
items.strategy: For F_s=[B_s→R(1)], split the surjection as graded right modules. Its kernel is generated by (alpha_s⊗1-1⊗alpha_s)/2 in internal degree +1 and is the graph bimodule R_s(-1); as a right module it is R(-1). Thus F_s retracts onto this kernel as a right-module complex. More generally the raw tensor product has bimodule cohomology R_x(-ell(x)): tensoring the rank-one graph kernels gives R_x and adds the shifts, while freeness on the needed sides makes the tensor product preserve the quasi-isomorphisms. To obtain a right-module homotopy equivalence, inductively tensor each split right-module retraction with the next B_s and R(1); these maps are right-linear and all terms are free, and R_x is right-free rank one. Removing contractible bimodule summands preserves that retraction. Right reduction preserves the right-module homotopy equivalence, so the reduced cohomology is one copy of R in internal degree ell(x). Apply this to the reduced expression xs and F_xF_s (homotopy equivalent to F_{xs}). There is no negative cohomological term, so the kernel of the first differential is exactly H^0, with no vector in internal degrees ≤ell(x). Canceling a contractible pair in cohomological degrees 1 and 2 leaves this injectivity intact. This injectivity is obtained before any HR argument. Then use the independent positive factorization identity and operator commutation, and the correctly graded HR target W with map into W(1), to invoke the weak-Lefschetz substitute. Do not claim HR for the unsplit zero-parameter descent target; use the theorem's d_3 separation.
